The multiple subscribe unit test was updated to reflect new (and correct) functionality.

Right now, there is a slight difference for QoS, as because each subscription has it's on QoS value, technically when we subscribe, we will use only the first QoS that was used.  Not only that, if MQTT disconnects/reconnects, the subscription it fines (based on the key filter) will be the winner for QoS.

It really doesn't make much sense to store QoS on a per-Subscription basis, as this should never have worked.  We were probably continually changing the QoS when we were sending multiple SUBSCRIBE calls earlier.

In other words, we are no worse off, but we should probably figure out how to handle QoS better in the future.  You can only have one QoS per topic regardless, so we may need to store QoS separately from the Subscribe classes.  And we will have to figure out what to do on subsequent subscriptions (do we re-subscribe if the QoS is different? do we ignore the new QoS value (which is what we are currently doing with this new patch), do we only re-subscribe if the QoS is higher?)

Though that is all beyond the scope of this PR.

@emontnemery 

> I'm closing this PR, the two suggested methods for improving startup time can be explored in separate PRs:
>     * Debounce subscribe calls

Don't forget to actually do the smart thing, and both deduplicate topic subscribes and make SINGLE subscribe calls (ie. subscribe((topic1, qos), (topic2, qos)) as opposed to a loop of individual subscribe calls.  There is no reason to loop through each topic and subscribe.

>     * Possibly do something smart with retained messages
>       
>       * What's currently in the PR is not correct, but on simple topics where we've received only a single retained message, I think we can replay that message to new subscribers instead of re-subscribing.

What is in this PR is:
1. Deliver all messages for wildcard topics to all subscribers to those wildcard topics - regardless of RETAIN (when you subscribe to a wildcard, it can and often will send a large number of RETAIN=1 calls - one for each topic matching that wildcard).
2. Deliver all messages of RETAIN=0 messages to all current subscribers on a topic (there is also no  guarantee a topic will have ANY RETAIN=1 messages - I found this out when I tried to say "don't process retain=0 messages until after you process a retain=1 message" = it failed because the zigbee sensors don't have a persisted status at all, so no retain=1 message)
3. Deliver only one RETAIN=1 message to any simple topic subscriber, ignore all future RETAIN=1 messages for that subscriber (in this case a subscribe is an individual entity - or an individual instance of the Subscribe class)
4. We CAN send multiple subscribes on a single topic due to the debounce (say you have 20 entities that use a topic, and 5 of them get in before the debounce triggers a subscribe, and the other 15 get in the next round - the RETAIN=1 message triggered for the first subscribe will be delivered to the first 5, or possibly up to all 20, the RETAIN=1 message triggered by the next debounce subscribe will only be delivered to those who didn't get the one from the previous subscribe.  RETAIN=0 is unaffected).

This IS correct - because the documentation says that a RETAIN=1 message is received only on a new subscription, and otherwise it will send RETAIN=0 messages.  If we are receiving a RETAIN=1 message, it's because we subscribed to a topic again (presumably for a new entity) - but the existing entities already got their "baseline status" and don't need to get it/process it again.
If a message is coming in because the publisher published a new message (regardless of RETAIN=1 or 0), we will receive the message with RETAIN=0 and send it to all subscribers using this PR's logic.

Funnily enough, what you're advocating of caching and skipping subscribes is exactly my FIRST solution, which you rejected for this exact reason, because it didn't handle RETAIN=1 messages correctly.  I fixed that, and now you want to "do something smart".  As you mentioned in your FIRST reply - there is no way to know if a topic has only received a single retained message. EACH subscribe call will result in a maximum of 1 RETAIN=1 message per subscribe to that topic.  Subsequent RETAIN=1 messages (from the publishing side) will come through as RETAIN=0, and any existing subscribed topic will have no way of knowing.  So no way of realistically caching it.

I guess you could do a small optimization of if (number of received messages on a simple topic == 1, and that message was RETAIN=1) skip re-subscribe.  That would work, but have no real difference to the current code except it foregoes that subscription - which is already not as much of an issue due to debouncing / deduplicating.  The current code already avoids the exponential re-processing of RETAIN=1 messages.

But, good luck.  It's your baby now.

> But, good luck. It's your baby now.

It isn't.

Locking this PR.

../Frenck

issue_context.title: MQTT device not subscribed on all entities
issue_context.body:
### The problem

I have a number of sensors that aren't getting updated, because the entities are not subscribed correctly.

I'm using Zigbee2MQTT -> Mosquitto -> Home Assistant.
These are all running individually in their own containers.

Looking at the entity for a closet door sensor, let's look at the 'contact' entity:
```
Office Closet Door contact (binary_sensor.office_closet_door_contact)
MQTT discovery data:

    Topic: homeassistant/binary_sensor/0xb0ce1814036d5a78/contact/config 
    Payload
      availability:
        - topic: zigbee2mqtt/bridge/state
          value_template: '{{ value_json.state }}'
      device:
        identifiers:
          - zigbee2mqtt_0xb0ce1814036d5a78
        manufacturer: Sengled
        model: Smart window and door sensor (E1D-G73WNA)
        name: Office Closet Door
      device_class: door
      name: Office Closet Door contact
      payload_off: true
      payload_on: false
      state_topic: zigbee2mqtt/Office Closet Door
      unique_id: 0xb0ce1814036d5a78_contact_zigbee2mqtt
      value_template: '{{ value_json.contact }}'
      platform: mqtt

Subscribed topics: 
  - zigbee2mqtt/bridge/state
```

Or, looking at the raw JSON:
```
Zigbee2MQTT:info  2023-02-12 17:49:47: MQTT publish: topic 'homeassistant/binary_sensor/0xb0ce1814036d5a78/contact/config', payload '{"availability":[{"topic":"zigbee2mqtt/bridge/state","value_template":"{{ value_json.state }}"}],"device":{"identifiers":["zigbee2mqtt_0xb0ce1814036d5a78"],"manufacturer":"Sengled","model":"Smart window and door sensor (E1D-G73WNA)","name":"Office Closet Door"},"device_class":"door","name":"Office Closet Door contact","payload_off":true,"payload_on":false,"state_topic":"zigbee2mqtt/Office Closet Door","unique_id":"0xb0ce1814036d5a78_contact_zigbee2mqtt","value_template":"{{ value_json.contact }}"}'
```

So you can see, it told the MQTT integration to subscribe to the zigbee2mqttt/Office Closet Door topic for updates - and it didn't.

I am getting events just fine on that topic:
```
Zigbee2MQTT:info  2023-02-12 18:10:26: MQTT publish: topic 'zigbee2mqtt/Office Closet Door', payload '{"battery":null,"battery_low":false,"contact":true,"linkquality":140,"tamper":false,"update":{"installed_version":-1,"latest_version":-1,"state":null},"update_available":null,"voltage":null}'
```

I also verified all this using the mqtt configure screen's listen functionality directly.  I'm receiving these events.  It's just that the entity did not subscribe to the correct topics when it created/configured the entity via. auto-creation.

I am sure I could add this sensor to the configuration.yaml myself, but I would rather not have to manually configure all my endpoints, that rather defeats the purpose.

Uhh - how is this not an issue with HA-MQTT?

I showed you the `homeassistant/binary_sensor/0xb0ce1814036d5a78/contact/config` topic contents that HA-MQTT received.

That topic clearly included that availability is on `zigbee2mqtt/bridge/state` and state is on `zigbee2mqtt/Office Closet Door`

**HA-MQTT did not process the config message correctly, and only subscribed the resulting entity to the availability topic, not the state topic**

It's not zigbee2mqtt's responsibility to subscribe HA-MQTT to topics, Just tell HA-MQTT what those topics are.

Additionally, zigbee2mqtt was sending the correct data on the state topic as it said it would.

**zigbee2mqtt is doing exactly what it said it would** - it sent the configuration information, with the correct information.  And then sent state information on the state topic.

This is absolutely the configuration part of HA-MQTT incorrectly parsing the config and not subscribing the entity in question to the state topic.

Heck - the information I provided for the contact entity, was **pulled from HA itself** (looking at 'MQTT Info' on the entity).  This shows that HA DID received the correct information, it just didn't do the right thing with it.

As an aside, just fobbing this off to Zigbee2MQTT when I have shown you everything **from the HA side** is lazy.

I showed you those Zigbee2MQTT publish messages because they were easy to grab.  But I also verified **the exact same messages are received by HA-MQTT** - by going to the MQTT configure screen and doing a listen on the state topic - and what do you know, the data is there.

Here is the patch that actually fixed the issue:

```
diff --git i/homeassistant/components/mqtt/client.py w/homeassistant/components/mqtt/client.py
index 28d60a5fdb..75337d9012 100644
--- i/homeassistant/components/mqtt/client.py
+++ w/homeassistant/components/mqtt/client.py
@@ -188,6 +188,53 @@ def wrap_msg_callback(

     return wrapper_func

+class TopicDedup:
+
+    message_callbacks: dict[str, MessageCallbackType]
+    remove: CALLBACK_TYPE = None
+    last_msg: str = None
+
+    def __init__(self):
+        self.message_callbacks = {}
+
+    async def add_subscription(self, callback: AsyncMessageCallbackType | MessageCallbackType) -> CALLBACK_TYPE:
+        id = str(uuid.uuid1())
+        self.message_callbacks[id] = catch_log_exception(
+                callback,
+                lambda msg: (
+                    f"Exception in {msg_callback.__name__} when handling msg on "
+                    f"'{msg.topic}': '{msg.payload}'"
+                ),
+            )
+
+        async def custom_remove() -> None:
+            del self.message_callbacks[id]
+
+            if len(self.message_callbacks) == 0:
+                await self.remove()
+                remove = None
+                last_msg = None
+
+        if self.last_msg is not None:
+            if asyncio.iscoroutinefunction(callback):
+                await callback(self.last_msg)
+            else:
+                callback(self.last_msg)
+
+        return custom_remove
+
+    async def callback(self, msg: ReceiveMessage) -> None:
+        self.last_msg = msg
+        for cb in self.message_callbacks.values():
+            if asyncio.iscoroutinefunction(cb):
+                await cb(msg)
+            else:
+                cb(msg)
+
+    def subscribers(self) -> int:
+        return len(self.message_callbacks)
+
+subscribed_topics: dict[str, TopicDedup] = {}

 @bind_hass
 async def async_subscribe(
@@ -233,18 +280,15 @@ async def async_subscribe(
             cast(DeprecatedMessageCallbackTypes, msg_callback)
         )

-    async_remove = await mqtt_data.client.async_subscribe(
-        topic,
-        catch_log_exception(
-            wrapped_msg_callback,
-            lambda msg: (
-                f"Exception in {msg_callback.__name__} when handling msg on "
-                f"'{msg.topic}': '{msg.payload}'"
-            ),
-        ),
-        qos,
-        encoding,
-    )
+    if topic not in subscribed_topics:
+        subscribed_topics[topic] = TopicDedup()
+    sub_topic = subscribed_topics.get(topic)
+    async_remove = await sub_topic.add_subscription(wrapped_msg_callback)
+    if sub_topic.subscribers() == 1:
+        sub_topic.remove = await mqtt_data.client.async_subscribe(
+            topic, sub_topic.callback, qos, encoding,
+        )
+
     return async_remove


```

Note - when I say 'block' below, I mean waiting on an async call with await, not a dead sleep.

As far as I know, the task creation just puts a task in the queue for the main HASS async loop (?) to execute - more or less immediately returning. This means that calling this with the lock is short lived because all it should really be doing is essentially some kind of hass.event_loop.tasks.append(coroutine) equivalent.  Which would be fairly quick.

The reason I want this separate is that many async_subscribe calls are going to be called back to back - as a side effect of discovery and entity creation.  Repeatedly and in sequence.  If one of them kicks off an actual subscribe call (due to the debunce time), which itself can block, then that sequence is paused until the subscribe call is completely finished.

Handing this off to HASS, means that, even in a single threaded mechanism, if a subscribe call initiates, when it blocks, it can go back to adding more subscriptions in it's sequence.  This leads to a higher chance that entities that share the same subscription topic (ie. entities on the same device) get collected into a single subscribe call, and not spread across multiple subscribe calls.  It also leads to a higher number of subscriptions being able to be done in a fewer number of calls (we can process more subscribe requests while waiting for the previous to complete).

If my understand of how async_create_task works is flawed, then yes, I would want this outside of the lock.  Though it was just easier to take advantage of the aforementioned if statement.

As for the lock - I only created it to ensure that it couldn't be modified by one entity doing a subscribe while the HASS task loop is clearing out that array, for processing it or unsub is deleting an entry from it.

3. A unsubscribes
  - Subscription for foo for A is removed.
  - pending for foo should NOT be removed (subscription for B exists).
4. B unsubscribes
  - Subscription for foo for B is removed.
  - pending for foo should be removed.
5. perform_async_subscribe is invoked - and doesn't subscribe to foo.

This can all happen before the pending subscription is processed due to the delay.
Without this code, the subscription entry for A and B would be removed.  But the pending subscription would still exist and we would still subscribe to that topic.

If I just blindly removed the pending subscription, and either B or A had not unsubscribed, we would never perform a subscription that was still needed.
